userStories.title: Add configurable item-publish pacing and safe rejection retries
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Parsing a config with no workflow.itemPublish block yields workflow.itemPublish equal to { writeGapMs: 1000, retryBackoffMs: 60000, maxRetries: 2, maxWaitMs: 300000 }, and WORKFLOW_ITEM_PUBLISH_DEFAULTS equals the same object.
[unit] Parsing workflow.itemPublish: { maxRetries: 5 } yields maxRetries: 5 with the other three keys at their defaults.
[unit] Parsing workflow.itemPublish.writeGapMs: -1 fails schema validation.

[unit] isRetryableRejection returns true for a NaxError with code FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED and context.stderr 'gh: You have exceeded a secondary rate limit and have been temporarily blocked from content creation.'.
[unit] isRetryableRejection returns true for a FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED error whose stderr is 'gh: Validation Failed (HTTP 422)'.
[unit] isRetryableRejection returns true for a FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED error whose stderr is 'gh: HTTP 429'.
[unit] isRetryableRejection returns false for a FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED error whose stderr is 'gh: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway'.
[unit] isRetryableRejection returns false for a NaxError with code FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE, and for a plain Error.
[unit] With _itemPublishPacerDeps.sleep stubbed, a pacer created with writeGapMs: 1000 runs its first write with no sleep and sleeps 1000 ms before its second write.
[unit] A write whose action throws a retryable rejection once and then resolves 'ok' resolves 'ok', after one sleep of retryBackoffMs, with the action called twice.
[unit] A write whose action always throws a retryable rejection, with maxRetries: 2, rejects with that rejection after the action was called 3 times.
[unit] A write whose action throws a FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE error rejects with that error after one call and no back-off sleep.

[unit] With writeGapMs: 10, retryBackoffMs: 100, maxWaitMs: 100, maxRetries: 2 and an action that always throws a retryable rejection, the first write rejects with that rejection after 2 calls (one 100 ms back-off; a second back-off would exceed the budget), and spent is then true.

[unit] Given the pacer from the previous criterion (writeGapMs:10, retryBackoffMs:100, maxWaitMs:100, maxRetries:2) after its first write spent the 100 ms wait budget and set spent:true, a second write (whose 10 ms gap would exceed the budget) rejects with NaxError code ITEM_PUBLISH_BUDGET_SPENT without calling its action.
[unit] A pacer created with maxWaitMs: 0 runs its first write (no wait needed) and resolves its result.

[unit] After the budget is spent (spent true), writeReserved still runs its action, and when that action throws a retryable rejection once and then resolves, writeReserved resolves after one back-off sleep and spent stays true.

[unit] A retried write called with { itemId: '_run:cv1' } logs a warn line '[item-threads] Write rejected; retrying after back-off' with itemId: '_run:cv1' and an attempt field equal to the retry number.
[unit] A write called with { retries: 0 } whose action throws a retryable rejection rejects after one call with no back-off sleep, even though the pacer's maxRetries is 2.

routing.reasoning: Introduces a stateful generic write abstraction with shared wait accounting, budget refusal, reserved writes, safe error classification, and schema/default integration; not an authentication or permission change.

suggestedCriteria: Parsing each workflow.itemPublish setting rejects fractional values and accepts zero.
isRetryableRejection returns false when FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED has absent or non-string stderr.
isRetryableRejection recognizes mixed-case RATE LIMIT, http 429, and http 422 stderr text.
A normal write permits a wait that makes cumulative waiting exactly maxWaitMs without setting spent.
writeReserved that takes cumulative waiting past maxWaitMs leaves a previously false spent value false.

`FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` gains rows for `workflow.itemPublish`, `workflow.itemPublish.writeGapMs`, `workflow.itemPublish.retryBackoffMs`, `workflow.itemPublish.maxRetries` and `workflow.itemPublish.maxWaitMs`, each one line on what it bounds, matching the existing `workflow.review.coverageRetries` rows.

the `workflow` config table gains four rows, `itemPublish.writeGapMs`, `itemPublish.retryBackoffMs`, `itemPublish.maxRetries` and `itemPublish.maxWaitMs`, each with its default and one line on what it bounds.

userStories.title: Pace item threads and reserve every index write
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] postItemThreads with a postable file-level item and forge deps whose first thread post fails with stderr 'gh: Validation Failed (HTTP 422)' and then succeeds, and _itemPublishPacerDeps.sleep stubbed, posts that thread (outcome posted includes it) after one back-off sleep of pacing.retryBackoffMs.
[integration] postItemThreads with forge deps whose w-index write fails once with a secondary-rate-limit stderr and then succeeds returns indexWritten: true and failed: 0.

[integration] postItemThreads sleeps pacing.writeGapMs between consecutive thread posts: with three postable items and writeGapMs: 1000, the stubbed sleep sees at least two calls of 1000 ms before the index write.

[integration] postItemThreads with maxWaitMs: 0, writeGapMs: 1 and three postable file-level items posts the first thread, counts the second (whose gap was refused) and the third as failed, does not call the forge for either, and logs one warn line '[item-threads] Pacing budget spent; skipping remaining threads' with skipped: 2.

[integration] postItemThreads with maxWaitMs: 0, writeGapMs: 1 and three postable items still attempts the w-index write after skipping the threads, and returns indexWritten: true when that write succeeds.

[integration] postItemThreads on a PR with no index comment, whose w-index post always fails with a retryable rejection, returns indexWritten: false and indexMissing: true after maxRetries + 1 index write calls.
[integration] postItemThreads on a PR that already has an own w-index comment, whose edit of it always fails, returns indexWritten: false and indexMissing: false.
[integration] postItemThreads whose w-index write fails with a non-retryable FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE error returns indexWritten: false after exactly one index write call.
[integration] postItemThreads whose initial PR read fails returns { posted: 0, closed: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 1, indexWritten: false, indexMissing: true }.

[integration] The feature environment's postItemThreads step, built from a config with workflow.itemPublish.writeGapMs: 7, passes pacing.writeGapMs: 7 to postItemThreads (stub the forge deps and observe the stubbed sleep receive 7 between two thread posts).
[integration] postItemThreads with no pacing in its input uses WORKFLOW_ITEM_PUBLISH_DEFAULTS (the stubbed sleep sees 1000 ms between two thread posts).
[integration] A closing reply in maintainItemIndex that fails once with a retryable rejection and then succeeds is counted in closed, not in failed.
[integration] A reopen reply in reopenReraisedItems that fails once with a retryable rejection and then succeeds reopens the item (it is not counted in failed).

[integration] postItemThreads for an item with file and line whose inline post fails with stderr 'gh: Validation Failed (HTTP 422)' calls the file-level postItemComment next with no back-off sleep between the two, and counts the item as posted when that succeeds.
[integration] When a file-level thread post remains rejected after maxRetries retries and the wait budget permits those retries, postItemThreads counts that item as failed.

routing.reasoning: Coordinates one shared pacer and mutable index state across posting, reopening, closure, and environment wiring, preserving ownership and partial-failure behavior.

suggestedCriteria: When a reopen pre-notice creates the first w-index successfully but the final index edit fails, postItemThreads returns indexWritten:false and indexMissing:false.
When the pacing budget is spent, postItemThreads does not include later owned or non-postable items in its failed count or budget-warning skipped count.
When a reopen invalidation index write exhausts its retries, reopenReraisedItems does not post the corresponding reopen notice.
When the final index write fails, maintainItemIndex does not send obsolete-thread closing replies or resolve writes.

userStories.title: Persist missing-index state and surface it at run end
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] postItemThreadsAfterPublish returns the outcome its postItemThreads step resolved, and returns undefined when the publish outcome is local-only.
[unit] publishStep whose env.steps.postItemThreads stub resolves indexMissing: true returns a patch with itemIndexMissing: true.

[unit] publishStep whose env.steps.postItemThreads stub resolves indexMissing: false returns a patch with itemIndexMissing: false, so a record that held true from an earlier publish reads false after it.
[unit] publishStep whose env.steps.postItemThreads stub throws returns a patch with no itemIndexMissing key.

[unit] The publish node of the feature graph accepts itemIndexMissing in its patch: running the graph's publish node with a stub that resolves indexMissing: true leaves itemIndexMissing: true on the record.
[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary for a record with itemIndexMissing: true and feature demo returns itemIndexMissing: { hint: 'nax workflow record -f demo' }.
[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary with no feature name, for a record with itemIndexMissing: true, returns itemIndexMissing: { hint: 'nax workflow record' }.
[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary for a record with no itemIndexMissing, or with itemIndexMissing: false, returns a view with no itemIndexMissing key.

[unit] The end-report Workflow summary: line for a view with itemIndexMissing: { hint: 'nax workflow record -f demo' } contains 'item index not written; bot commands will refuse this PR (nax workflow record -f demo)'.

routing.reasoning: Although several files change, this story uses existing best-effort publish, graph-patch, and conditional-summary patterns for additive field plumbing; single-session TDD can verify true/false/omitted propagation and output without introducing a new abstraction.

suggestedCriteria: When a record already has itemIndexMissing:true and the thread step is absent, executing the graph's publish node preserves itemIndexMissing:true.
When the thread outcome is indexWritten:false,indexMissing:false because the old index remains, publishStep writes itemIndexMissing:false.

modifiedFiles.reason: `expectedProduces.publish` (lines 57-86) pins the `publish` node's produced fields and line 109 compares them with `toEqual`; US-003 adds `itemIndexMissing` to the node, so the pinned list gains `"itemIndexMissing"` and is otherwise unchanged.

userStories.title: Show missing indexes and recorded rulings in workflow status
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] workflowStatusCommand --json for a draft run whose live read fails, with a newest sidecar holding a waived decision for open item _run:cv1, reports settledItems containing { id: '_run:cv1', disposition: 'waived' } and an openItems list without _run:cv1.

[integration] workflowStatusCommand --json for a draft run whose live read fails, with a newest sidecar present, keeps source: 'run-record' and liveError, and has decisions equal to the sidecar path relative to the project directory.
[integration] workflowStatusCommand --json for a draft run whose live read fails, with a sidecar whose outcome is promoted, reports outcome: 'ready'.

[integration] workflowStatusCommand --json for a draft run whose live read fails reports outcome: 'ready' when the newest sidecar's outcome is verified-ready; with pending or abandoned it keeps the record's outcome: 'draft'.
[integration] When workflowStatusCommand's live read fails, a newest-sidecar entry that settles a supplementary item removes it from supplementaryItems and lists it in settledItems.

[integration] When workflowStatusCommand's live read fails, a newest-sidecar decision whose id is neither an open nor a supplementary item is ignored: the report still settles the other entries and the command exits as it would without that entry.
[integration] A live read that fails and a newest sidecar that does not parse yield the run-record report with liveError and no decisions key.
[integration] workflowStatusCommand --json for a run whose record has itemIndexMissing: true reports itemIndexMissing: true.

[integration] The plain output for a run whose record has itemIndexMissing: true includes the line 'item index not written; settle items with nax workflow record -f <feature>' with the feature name filled in.
[integration] A run whose live read succeeds ignores any sidecar: settledItems comes from the live read alone and the report has no decisions key.

[integration] For a draft run whose live read fails, whose open items are a cannot-verify item and the CI item, and whose promoted sidecar settles the cannot-verify item, workflowStatusCommand reports no open items (the CI item is removed because the outcome is ready) and exits 0.
[integration] When workflowStatusCommand's live read fails, a newest-sidecar entry whose kind is finding for an open item of kind cannot-verify does not settle that item.

[integration] When workflowStatusCommand's live read fails, a confirmed newest-sidecar entry of kind advisor for an open advisor item settles it: the item is listed in settledItems with disposition confirmed and removed from openItems.
[integration] A run whose record has itemIndexMissing: false reports no itemIndexMissing key.

routing.reasoning: Extends one existing read-only CLI report using existing sidecar/loader APIs and deterministic id/kind filtering, with an adjacent command-level test file; no new persistence or security mechanism.

suggestedCriteria: When the newest sidecar is malformed and an older sidecar is readable, workflowStatusCommand applies neither sidecar and reports no decisions key.
When a live read succeeds for a run with itemIndexMissing:true, workflowStatusCommand still reports itemIndexMissing:true from the record.
When a live read fails with no sidecar present and no missing-index flag, workflowStatusCommand returns the existing record-only report with liveError and no decisions or itemIndexMissing keys.

analysis:
Goal and scope: close #2886 by pacing and selectively retrying post-publish item-thread writes, preserving an attempt to write the bot-required w-index, making a genuinely missing index visible in persisted workflow results and human-facing reports, and using recorded decisions when the live status read fails. The binding implementation order is US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 -> US-004, all with workdir packages/nax. US-001 also updates the repository-root configuration guide as explicitly required by the spec; retain its binding package workdir. No other workspace package, transport, agent dispatch policy, release version, or permission logic needs modification. This is an enhancement of existing TypeScript/Bun code, not a greenfield subsystem. Graph navigation tools are unavailable in this session; discovery used direct reads and text searches at the supplied repository root. These findings cite inspected source locations, rather than relying only on the spec's baseline line numbers.

US-001 architecture and files: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-workflow.ts:16-23 provides the nested Zod .prefault({}) and parsed WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS pattern. WorkflowConfigObjectSchema starts at :25 and includes review at :40; add the itemPublish schema there with nonnegative integer writeGapMs=1000, retryBackoffMs=60000, maxRetries=2, maxWaitMs=300000. packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-workflow.ts:40 defines WorkflowConfig and :65 its optional review field: itemPublish must likewise remain optional for hand-built configurations. Export WORKFLOW_ITEM_PUBLISH_DEFAULTS as the parsed schema defaults, not a second hand-maintained object. packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:167-169 re-exports workflow defaults; expose the new default through the same public config boundary if consumers use that barrel. Avoid a runtime config/workflow import cycle when sharing ItemPublishConfig: type-only imports are erased, and schema/default ownership stays in config. packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:106-108 holds the existing workflow.review descriptions; add the block and four leaf descriptions. docs/guides/configuration.md:1071 starts the Workflow section and :1114 is in its config key table; add four documented default/bound rows there. packages/nax/test/unit/config/workflow-config.test.ts:11 pins the entire parsed workflow object with toEqual: add only the new default block to that object and retain all existing fields.

Create packages/nax/src/workflow/item-publish-pacer.ts and packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/item-publish-pacer.test.ts. Use NaxError from the existing error boundary (packages/nax/src/errors.ts:7-9) and getLogger's structured warn convention already used in packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-post.ts:51-55. The new ITEM_PUBLISH_BUDGET_SPENT is an error code string, not a reason to alter shared agent errors. packages/nax/src/forge/comments.ts:32-48 is deliberately a single-attempt runForgeWrite: a nonzero exit creates FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED with trimmed context.stderr, while an invalid success body creates FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE. Leave this shared layer unchanged: all seven helpers already call it, and global retry there could duplicate uncertain writes and broaden the scope to bot/promote operations. Classify only NaxError FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED whose stderr contains rate limit, HTTP 429, or HTTP 422 case-insensitively. Other 4xx/auth errors, 5xx, timeouts, plain errors, and unparseable successes do not qualify. The 422 policy deliberately accepts wasted retries on permanent file-level validation failures because gh hides the detail. Inject sleep through _itemPublishPacerDeps using cancellableDelay (packages/nax/src/utils/bun-deps.ts:72); packages/nax/src/workflow/ci-wait.ts:20 and :55 show the existing delay dependency seam. No real clock or network is needed to test the pacer. Gap is once at entry to each write after the first; retries repeat only the action after back-off, not the gap. Track cumulative requested waits, not action execution duration. Refuse a normal wait only when total + wait exceeds maxWaitMs, allow equality and no-wait actions, set spent on budget refusal, and retain the original rejection when refusing a retry. Reserved writes count their waits but never set spent, never refuse for budget, and remain retry-bounded.

US-002 write ownership and integration: packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-post.ts:27-41 defines ItemThreadsInput/Outcome; add optional pacing and required indexWritten/indexMissing. :66-81 implements inline, same-file fallback, then anchor fallback; retain that ordering and existing behavior, wrapping inline in write with retries:0 and file-level calls in normal write. Inline fallback has no back-off, although it still observes the normal inter-write gap. :85-104 deliberately completes ownership reads before any write: preserve that duplicate-prevention property and leave all readers unpaced. :106-147 creates the ownership set, iterates postable/non-CI items, then reopens and maintains the index. Create exactly one pacer per invocation and pass it in PostingContext, IndexContext, and ReopenContext; do not give each helper a separate budget. attempt at :58 catches every error, so use pacer.spent after a failed post to stop later postable/unowned thread posts. Count the current failed item exactly once, count only later postable/unowned items as additional failures, retain skipped accounting for non-postable/owned items, and emit the single budget warning with its skipped count.

packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-index.ts:10-19 holds mutable postedIndex alongside the ownership snapshot. writeItemIndex at :49-60 edits read.indexComment or a newly postedIndex, otherwise posts and stores the comment id. Every such index write must use writeReserved, including the pre-notice call made by reopenReraisedItems. maintainItemIndex at :62-93 currently writes the index before obsolete closing replies/resolves and refuses closures after an index failure. Preserve that ordering and failure behavior, return indexed with closed/failed, and wrap each closing forge action individually in normal write. packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-reopen.ts:78-93 persists pending reopen invalidation through writeItemIndex before posting a notice and unresolving. Preserve the durable pre-notice ordering and share the same maintenance object between reopen and final index maintenance so postedIndex survives the pre-notice call. Wrap replyToThread and unresolveThread individually, not an entire multi-write sequence that could replay an already completed action. indexWritten reflects only the final index write. indexMissing distinguishes no index from a stale one: an initial index comment or any successful pre-notice creation prevents missing=true even if the final edit fails. The initial-read failure is explicitly required to return indexWritten:false,indexMissing:true, despite an incomplete snapshot. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-env.ts:111-112 currently captures projectDir/feature but no pacing; add pacing:fc.workflow.itemPublish without losing those identity overrides. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:44 already types its optional step as Promise<ItemThreadsOutcome>, so adding required outcome fields reaches all stubs.

US-002 tests and compatibility: packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/item-threads-post.test.ts:52-85 has a ForgeDeps harness and :96 an outcome helper; extend that helper with default indexWritten:true,indexMissing:false and parameters for unwritten cases, retaining the other existing assertions. Its :100-119 logger hooks can also install/restore the injected sleep. Add immediate sleep seams to the existing item-threads-index.test.ts and item-threads-reopen.test.ts suites without changing their assertions. Update the result stubs in packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/publish-item-threads.test.ts:16 and :213 and packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/finalize-approval-failures.test.ts:350 with indexWritten:true,indexMissing:false. packages/nax/test/integration/workflow/publish-item-threads.test.ts:55-65 asserts the real environment step and initial-read-failure result; extend only that expected result and add the configured pacing observation there. Integration scenarios should invoke real postItemThreads with stubbed ForgeDeps.run and injected sleep, exercising NaxError creation by the real forge helpers rather than bypassing the seam. Keep all waits virtual and restore mutable dependencies after each test. Existing GitHub/GitLab anchoring, ownership, reopen, and reviewed-head behavior must remain intact.

US-003 propagation: packages/nax/src/workflow/publish-item-threads.ts:22-29 currently returns Promise<void> and guards no step/no URL/non-PR outcomes; :31-35 guards identity; :50-67 awaits the post, writes a ledger note, and swallows failures. Return the actual ItemThreadsOutcome on success and undefined for every existing no-op/error path without turning this best-effort reporting step into a failed publish. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-steps.ts:431-486 currently discards that return value at :441; capture it and conditionally spread itemIndexMissing:outcome.indexMissing into the patch. Do not infer it from indexWritten:false, because a stale index remains usable by bot commands. A successful later publish writes false to clear a previous true, while an absent outcome preserves the old record field. Add optional itemIndexMissing?:boolean to packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:231's WorkflowFeatureRecord, and add it to the publish node's produces list in packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-graph.ts:95-117. The spec's rationale about undefined patches is imprecise relative to the current runner: packages/nax/src/step-graph/run.ts:75-82 rejects undeclared keys, including explicitly undefined keys; :140-153 deletes a declared key whose patch value is undefined. Either way, conditional omission is mandatory here to preserve earlier evidence. No change to the generic graph runner is needed. packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-graph.test.ts:57-86 pins produces and :109 compares the lists: add only itemIndexMissing.

packages/nax/src/workflow/run-summary.ts:73-77's ciRemainingOf and :79-113's conditional view construction are the reporting patterns to extend. packages/nax/src/log-format/types.ts:82-111 owns WorkflowSummaryView; add optional itemIndexMissing?:{hint:string}|undefined, including the key only for record true. The hint is nax workflow record -f <feature>, or nax workflow record without a feature. packages/nax/src/execution/workflow-end-report.ts:33-51 builds the Workflow summary: log message and :61-63 logs both the text and structured view. Add the exact required missing-index phrase there; existing lines must remain unchanged when the flag is absent/false. Its view is also passed to the headless footer at :253-255. packages/nax/src/log-format/workflow-summary.ts:36-72 is a separate footer renderer; the explicit AC targets the Workflow summary: end-report line, so do not replace that obligation with a footer-only change. Extend the existing publish-item-threads, feature-graph, run-summary, and execution/workflow-end-report unit suites; inspected summary fixtures are at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/run-summary.test.ts:15-47 and packages/nax/test/unit/execution/workflow-end-report.test.ts:35-49.

US-004 status architecture: packages/nax/src/cli/workflow.ts:53-73 defines the JSON report; :85-102's reportFor builds the record-only fields and :105-122's buildReport selects the live/fallback branch. Surface itemIndexMissing:true only when record.itemIndexMissing===true, irrespective of live-read success; never emit false or undefined-valued keys. Only the failed live-read branch applies newestSidecar(loaded.runDir), adding relative(dir,found.path) as decisions while preserving source:run-record and liveError. Leave today's eligibility for live reads and the successful live branch unchanged. packages/nax/src/workflow/live-status.ts:63-92 returns a run-record fallback both on read errors and on a missing w-index (:78); this module need not change. packages/nax/src/workflow/run-verdict.ts:24-35's LoadedRun already includes runDir, openItems, and supplementaryItems; its loader :83-107 fills story states and returns the authoritative items. Do not invent a second result-file discovery path. packages/nax/src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts:32-51 defines entry/sidecar types, :147-149 maps ruling to advisor, and :274-279 loads only the newest sidecar or throws for an invalid newest one. Reuse newestSidecar and sidecarKindFor by relative leaf imports to respect the import-cycle warning in packages/nax/src/cli/workflow.ts:9-13. Read-only references such as forge/comments.ts, live-status.ts, decisions-sidecar.ts, bun-deps.ts, and run-verdict.ts are integration context, not instructions to broaden mutations.

For the fallback, match decisions by id plus sidecarKindFor(item)===entry.kind against both open and supplementary items. Settled entries contribute only {id,disposition} and are removed from the corresponding list. Ignore unmatched/mismatched entries individually; do not reuse checkEntriesAgainstItems (packages/nax/src/workflow/decisions-sidecar.ts:164-181), which throws on mismatches and is intentionally stricter for record/promote callers. A confirmed advisor decision settles offline, unlike live-status partition at :39-43, where an advisor may still await a fix-closing reply. For promoted or verified-ready, set report outcome ready and remove CI_ITEM_ID from openItems (packages/nax/src/workflow/open-items.ts:16 defines _run:ci). Pending and abandoned leave the record verdict alone. Malformed newest sidecars degrade to the existing record report with liveError, no decisions, and no attempt to apply an older file. Preserve the exit rule in packages/nax/src/cli/workflow.ts:126-128: only ready with no open items exits 0; supplementary items never block. printPlain at :154-166 must print the missing-index line before its early return for no supplementary items. Do not show an offline CI waiver or change source to a new value.

Create packages/nax/test/unit/cli/workflow-status-sidecar.test.ts as specified, even though its public-command scenarios are tagged integration. Existing adjacent tests supply fixtures: packages/nax/test/unit/cli/workflow-status.test.ts:22-69 captures CLI output and writes result files in withTempDir; packages/nax/test/unit/cli/workflow-status-live.test.ts:37-49 builds draft records and :120-145 stubs forge responses. Keep existing successful-live and no-sidecar report shapes unchanged. New tests should write real decisions sidecars/results in a temporary run directory, inject offline or successful forge responses, call workflowStatusCommand, and inspect JSON/plain output and return codes.

Risks and migration: default pacing introduces real publish latency and retry waits; all affected tests must stub sleep. maxWaitMs bounds cumulative ordinary waiting, not total wall-clock publish time: reserved index writes may exceed it and closing writes after an index may then refuse. Permanent file-level 422s intentionally burn the budget; inline 422s must not. Shared write-level retries must not replay a compound successful notice or closure sequence. Missing-versus-stale index and the pre-notice postedIndex state are the main correctness traps. Optional config and persisted fields make old configuration/result records readable without a schema-version bump or backfill; hand-built workflow blocks need parsed-default fallback. Required outcome fields do require coordinated updates to typed/untyped stubs in US-002 before downstream consumption in US-003. Status must be read-only and fail soft for sidecar read/parse failure without changing record/promote validation semantics. No repair command or historical re-publication is included. Failure-handling rows are covered by US-001's retry/logging/nonretry/budget ACs, US-002's inline fallback, exhausted-thread/index retry, skip and missing/stale index ACs, US-003's record/summary ACs, and US-004's malformed-sidecar and unknown/mismatched-entry ACs.
